examples.ko: 병아리들이 삐악삐악 소리를 내며 어미 닭을 따라가요.
examples.en: The chicks follow the mother hen, peeping away.

examples.ko: 아이가 병아리 흉내를 내면서 삐악삐악 말했어요.
examples.en: The child imitated a chick and said 'peep-peep.'

examples.ko: 상자 안에서 삐악삐악 하는 소리가 계속 들려요.
examples.en: I keep hearing a peeping sound from inside the box.

examples.ko: 시골 할머니 댁 마당에서 병아리가 삐악삐악 울어요.
examples.en: Chicks are cheeping in the yard of my grandmother's house in the countryside.
When I gave them food, the chicks gathered around, cheeping.

examples.ko: 아침부터 삐악삐악 소리가 나서 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: A peeping sound woke me up from early morning.

explain: 주로 병아리 소리에 써요. 다 큰 닭은 '꼬꼬댁', 수탉은 '꼬끼오'처럼 소리 표현이 달라져요. 동요나 동화에 자주 나오고, 아이에게 말할 때도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used mostly for the sound of chicks. A grown hen is '꼬꼬댁' and a rooster is '꼬끼오', so the sound words change. It often appears in children's songs and stories and is common when talking to kids.

examples.en: Your shirt is sticking out of your pants.
Some hair was sticking out of the hat.

examples.ko: 김밥 속 재료가 옆으로 삐져나와서 먹기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The filling is squeezing out of the side of the gimbap, so it's hard to eat.
If your feet stick out of the blanket, they get cold.
The bag is small, so things keep sticking out.

examples.ko: 빵 사이에서 크림이 삐져나오지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful so the cream doesn't squeeze out from between the bread.

explain: 틈이나 가장자리로 조금 튀어나온 모습에 써요. 옷, 머리카락, 속 재료처럼 안쪽에 있어야 할 것이 밖으로 나왔을 때 자연스러워요. '삐죽 나오다'와 비슷하지만, 안에 있던 것이 밀려 나온 느낌이 더 있어요.
explain_en: It describes something poking out slightly through a gap or edge, like clothes, hair or filling that should be inside. It is close to '삐죽 나오다', but it has more of a feel of something that was inside being pushed out.

examples.en: My younger sibling sulked because they couldn't get the toy.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 말에 삐쳐서 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: My friend is sulking over what I said and won't talk to me.

examples.ko: 별것도 아닌 일로 자꾸 삐치지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't keep sulking over trivial things.

examples.ko: 남자친구가 삐친 것 같은데 어떻게 풀어 줘야 할까요?
examples.en: My boyfriend seems sulky. How should I make it up to him?

examples.ko: 아이가 삐치면 한참 동안 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: When my child sulks, he doesn't talk for quite a while.
He's really sulking, so apologize first.

explain: 크게 화내는 것보다 서운해서 말을 안 하거나 토라지는 가벼운 감정이에요. 친구, 연인, 가족처럼 가까운 사이에서 많이 쓰고, 말할 때는 '삐지다'라고도 자주 해요. 비슷한 '토라지다'와 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a mild feeling of being hurt and going quiet, not full-blown anger. It is used among close people like friends, partners and family, and in speech people often say '삐지다' too. '토라지다' is a close synonym.

examples.ko: 중고 물건을 사고팔 수 있는 앱이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many apps where you can buy and sell secondhand items.
At the market, merchants buy and sell goods.
You have to be careful when buying and selling stocks.
In the old days, people bought and sold goods with rice.

examples.ko: 친구와 중고 옷을 사고팔다 보니 용돈이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Buying and selling used clothes with my friend increased my pocket money.

examples.ko: 외국에서는 물건을 사고팔 때 그 나라 돈을 써야 해요.
examples.en: When you buy and sell things abroad, you have to use that country's money.

explain: '사다'와 '팔다'가 합쳐진 말이라서 사는 쪽과 파는 쪽을 함께 말할 때 써요. 중고 거래, 주식, 시장 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 한 사람이 사기만 하거나 팔기만 할 때는 '사다'나 '팔다'를 따로 써요.
explain_en: It combines '사다' (buy) and '팔다' (sell), so use it when you talk about both sides of trading. It often appears with secondhand deals, stocks and markets. If someone only buys or only sells, use '사다' or '팔다' alone.

en: beef leg bone; beef shank bone

examples.en: I boiled the beef leg bones all day long.
On cold days, I think of bone broth soup.
I bought a pound of beef leg bones at the market.

examples.ko: 사골은 핏물을 먼저 빼고 끓여야 해요.
examples.en: You have to remove the blood from the bones before boiling them.

examples.ko: 엄마가 사골 육수로 떡국을 끓여 주셨어요.
examples.en: Mom made tteokguk with bone broth for me.

examples.ko: 사골 국물에 밥을 말아 먹으면 든든해요.
examples.en: Eating rice in bone broth is very filling.

explain: 보통 뼈 자체보다 '사골국', '사골 육수'처럼 오래 끓인 국물 이야기로 많이 말해요. 뽀얗고 진한 국물이 나오고, 떡국이나 국수의 육수로도 써요. 집에서는 오래 끓이는 음식이라 '사골을 고다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: People usually talk about it as '사골국' or '사골 육수', the long-simmered broth, rather than the bone itself. The broth turns milky and rich, and is also used as a base for tteokguk or noodles. Since it takes long to cook, people say '사골을 고다' (to simmer bones down).

examples.en: The flames are gradually dying down.

examples.ko: 그 이야기에 대한 관심이 금세 사그라졌어요.
examples.en: Interest in that story faded quickly.
As time passes, my anger subsides a little.
My fever didn't go down, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 인기가 사그라지기 전에 앨범을 내고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to release an album before my popularity fades.

examples.ko: 소문이 사그라질 때까지 조용히 기다려 보세요.
examples.en: Wait quietly until the rumor dies down.

explain: 불, 열, 화, 관심, 인기처럼 세게 일던 기운이 서서히 약해질 때 써요. '사그라들다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요. 단순히 아래로 내려오는 '가라앉다'보다, 기세가 점점 줄어드는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is used when something that was strong, like fire, fever, anger, interest or popularity, gradually weakens. '사그라들다' is a common variant. Compared with '가라앉다' (settle down), it stresses the force slowly shrinking.

examples.ko: 감기 때문에 사나흘 동안 학교에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't go to school for three or four days because of a cold.
I'm planning to go on a trip for three or four days.

examples.ko: 이 김치는 사나흘 뒤에 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: This kimchi tastes good after three or four days.
It has been raining for three or four days straight.
The item you ordered will arrive in three or four days.

examples.ko: 일이 많아서 사나흘은 밤을 새워야 해요.
examples.en: I have so much work that I'll need to stay up nights for three or four days.

explain: 사흘이나 나흘쯤 되는 기간을 대충 말할 때 써요. 정확한 숫자보다 '대략 그 정도'라는 느낌이라서 일정이나 기간을 말할 때 편해요. 같은 느낌으로 '이삼일', '삼사일'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a period of roughly three or four days, so it feels approximate rather than exact, which is handy for schedules. '이삼일' and '삼사일' give a similar feel.

examples.en: A new boy moved in next door.
Maybe because he's a boy, he's really active.
I'm so busy raising two boys.
The hospital told us it's a boy.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 사내아이보다 여자아이가 더 많아요.
examples.en: In our class, there are more girls than boys.
Boys are kicking a ball in the park.

explain: '남자아이'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만 조금 더 예스럽고 부모 세대가 자주 써요. 요즘 일상 대화에서는 '남자아이'가 더 흔해요. 짝이 되는 말은 '여자아이'예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '남자아이' but sounds a bit more old-fashioned and is used more by the parent generation. In everyday talk today, '남자아이' is more common. The counterpart is '여자아이'.

examples.en: I called a ladder truck early in the morning on moving day.

examples.ko: 사다리차가 있으면 높은 층에도 짐을 옮기기 쉬워요.
examples.en: With a ladder truck, it's easy to move things to high floors.
The ladder truck fee depends on the floor.
A ladder truck is parked in front of the apartment.
The workers loaded the refrigerator onto the ladder truck.
If you want to use a ladder truck, book it in advance.

explain: 우리나라에서는 높은 층으로 이삿짐을 올리고 내릴 때 쓰는 차를 가장 먼저 떠올려요. '사다리차를 부르다', '사다리차를 쓰다'처럼 말하고, 엘리베이터가 작거나 짐이 클 때 많이 이용해요. 소방차의 사다리차도 같은 이름으로 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: In Korea, people first think of the truck used to lift and lower moving goods to high floors. You say '사다리차를 부르다' or '사다리차를 쓰다', and it is popular when the elevator is small or items are big. Fire department ladder trucks can also be called by the same name.

examples.en: My wisdom tooth is coming in and my gums hurt.
Yesterday I went to the dentist and had my wisdom tooth pulled.

examples.ko: 사랑니를 뽑고 나서 하루 종일 죽만 먹었어요.
examples.en: After getting my wisdom tooth pulled, I only ate porridge all day.

examples.ko: 사랑니는 어른이 되어서 나는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Wisdom teeth often come in once you're an adult.
I heard my lower wisdom tooth grew in at a slant.
It's hard to eat because of my wisdom tooth.

explain: '사랑니가 나다', '사랑니를 뽑다'가 가장 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 치과에서는 '사랑니 발치'라고도 해요. 영어의 wisdom tooth처럼 '지혜'가 아니라 '사랑'이라는 말이 들어가서 재미있게 외울 수 있어요.
explain_en: The most common pairings are '사랑니가 나다' (a wisdom tooth comes in) and '사랑니를 뽑다' (pull a wisdom tooth). At the dentist it's also called '사랑니 발치'. Unlike English 'wisdom', the Korean word has 'love' in it, which makes it fun to remember.

examples.en: The ice cream melts softly in my mouth.
The snow melted away as soon as it touched my palm.
As I got sleepy, my eyes slowly closed.

examples.ko: 초콜릿이 혀 위에서 사르르 녹는 느낌이 좋아요.
examples.en: I like the feeling of chocolate melting on my tongue.
The tangled knot came loose easily.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 국물을 마시니 긴장이 사르르 풀렸어요.
examples.en: After drinking the hot soup, my tension melted away.

explain: '녹다', '풀리다', '감기다'처럼 부드럽게 저절로 변하는 말과 자주 같이 써요. 힘을 주지 않았는데 스르르 되는 느낌이에요. 음식이 입에서 부드럽게 녹을 때도 아주 자연스럽게 말해요.
explain_en: It pairs often with verbs like '녹다' (melt), '풀리다' (come undone) and '감기다' (close), for something that happens gently by itself. It gives a sense of changing smoothly with no effort. It is very natural for food that melts softly in your mouth.

examples.en: My father works as an office clerk at a small company.
I saw a notice saying they're hiring an office clerk.
The office clerk is organizing documents.
I asked the school office clerk for a certificate.
Attention to detail is important in office clerk work.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 병원에는 사무원이 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: The clinic in my neighborhood has two office staff.

explain: 책상에서 서류, 접수, 회계 같은 일을 하는 사람을 직업으로 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '회사원', '직원', '사무직'이라고 더 자주 말해요. 직접 부를 때는 '사무원님' 대신 이름이나 직함을 써요.
explain_en: It names the job of someone who does desk work such as paperwork, reception or accounting. In daily speech, people more often say '회사원', '직원' or '사무직'. When addressing someone directly, use their name or title rather than '사무원님'.

en: being in all directions; being all over the place; everywhere

examples.en: The rumor quickly spread in every direction.
I ran around everywhere to find my lost wallet.
The sound of firecrackers comes from all around.
I looked everywhere, but the key isn't there.

examples.ko: 길이 사방팔방으로 뚫려 있어서 어디든 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Roads run in every direction, so you can get anywhere.
Ads are plastered all over the place.

explain: '여기저기'와 비슷하지만 모든 방향이라는 과장된 느낌이 더 강해요. 소문이 퍼지거나, 뭔가를 찾아 헤매거나, 소리가 사방에서 들릴 때 자주 써요. 보통 '사방팔방으로', '사방팔방에서', '사방팔방 뛰어다니다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '여기저기' but has a stronger, exaggerated feel of every direction. It is often used for spreading rumors, searching all over, or sound coming from all sides. Typical forms are '사방팔방으로', '사방팔방에서' and '사방팔방 뛰어다니다'.

en: future son-in-law; prospective son-in-law; potential son-in-law

examples.ko: 여자친구 부모님은 저를 좋은 사윗감이라고 생각하세요.
examples.en: My girlfriend's parents think I'd make a good son-in-law.
My mother wants a sincere son-in-law for her daughter.

examples.ko: 저 청년이 아버지 마음에 쏙 드는 사윗감이래요.
examples.en: I heard that young man is just the kind of son-in-law my father likes.

examples.ko: 사윗감으로는 착하고 책임감 있는 사람이 좋아요.
examples.en: As a son-in-law, I'd like someone kind and responsible.

examples.ko: 내일 딸이 사윗감 될 사람을 데리고 와요.
examples.en: Tomorrow my daughter is bringing the person who may become my son-in-law.

examples.ko: 요즘은 직업보다 성격을 보고 사윗감을 골라요.
examples.en: These days people choose a son-in-law by personality rather than job.

explain: '-감'은 어떤 자격이 될 만한 사람을 뜻해서, 아직 사위가 아닌 후보를 말해요. '신랑감', '며느릿감'도 같은 짜임이에요. 이미 결혼한 후에는 그냥 '사위'라고 해요.
explain_en: The ending '-감' marks someone who could fill a role, so this refers to a candidate who isn't yet a son-in-law. '신랑감' and '며느릿감' follow the same pattern. After the marriage, you simply say '사위'.

examples.en: At the typhoon news, people stockpiled ramyeon.
The supermarket has no toilet paper because of panic buying.
Panic buying harms other people.

examples.ko: 물건이 부족해질까 봐 사재기하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people hoard because they fear a shortage.

examples.ko: 가격이 오르기 전에 사재기에 나선 사람들이 있었어요.
examples.en: Some people started stockpiling before prices rose.
Don't hoard; buy only what you need.

explain: 필요 이상으로 많이 사서 쌓아 두는 것이라 보통 좋지 않은 느낌으로 말해요. 뉴스에서는 태풍, 가격 인상, 물건 부족 같은 상황에서 자주 나와요. 동사로는 '사재기하다'라고 써요.
explain_en: It means buying far more than you need and piling it up, so it carries a negative tone. In the news it appears often with typhoons, price hikes and shortages. The verb form is '사재기하다'.

examples.en: The child pleaded for me to buy the toy.

examples.ko: 친구에게 한 번만 도와 달라고 사정사정해요.
examples.en: I'm begging my friend to help me just once.
Even though I begged, I only heard that it's not allowed.

examples.ko: 늦게 와서 문 좀 열어 달라고 사정사정하는 중이에요.
examples.en: I came late and am pleading with them to open the door.

examples.ko: 그렇게 사정사정하지 말고 이유부터 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't beg like that, and tell me the reason first.

examples.ko: 동생이 사정사정해서 할 수 없이 빌려줬어요.
examples.en: My sibling begged so much that I had no choice but to lend it.

explain: '사정하다'를 반복해서 더 간절하고 끈질기게 부탁하는 느낌이에요. 보통 '~해 달라고 사정사정하다'로 쓰고, '부탁하다'보다 훨씬 애원하는 말투예요. '빌다'나 '애원하다'와 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: Repeating '사정' makes the begging feel more desperate and persistent. It is usually used as '~해 달라고 사정사정하다' and is much more pleading than '부탁하다'. '빌다' and '애원하다' are close in feel.

en: saju; four pillars of destiny; fate

examples.en: I went to a fortune teller to have my sajupalja read.
They said I have a lot of water in my sajupalja.

examples.ko: 사주팔자는 태어난 해, 달, 날, 시간으로 본대요.
examples.en: I heard sajupalja is read from the year, month, day and hour of birth.

examples.ko: 사주팔자를 믿는 사람도 있고 안 믿는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people believe in sajupalja and some don't.

examples.ko: 사주팔자 탓하지 말고 직접 노력해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't blame your fate; try working at it yourself.

examples.ko: 친구가 사주팔자를 봐 줬는데 신기하게 잘 맞았어요.
examples.en: My friend read my sajupalja, and it was strangely accurate.

explain: 태어난 연, 월, 일, 시로 운명을 보는 전통적인 방법을 말하고, 타고난 운명이라는 뜻으로 넓게 쓰기도 해요. '사주를 보다', '사주팔자를 믿다'처럼 말하고, 줄여서 그냥 '사주'라고도 자주 해요. 대화에서는 '팔자'만 따로 써서 인생의 운을 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the traditional way of reading fate from the year, month, day and hour of birth, and is also used loosely for one's destiny. People say '사주를 보다' or '사주팔자를 믿다', and often shorten it to '사주'. In conversation, '팔자' alone is also used to talk about one's life luck.

examples.en: I went to an exhibition by a famous photographer.
I want to become a photographer.

examples.ko: 사진작가님이 사진을 아주 멋지게 찍어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The photographer took wonderful pictures for us.

examples.ko: 그 사진작가는 자연 풍경을 주로 찍어요.
examples.en: That photographer mainly shoots natural landscapes.
I went on an outdoor shoot with a photographer.
What should I do to become a photographer?

explain: 사진을 작품으로 찍는 사람이라는 느낌이 있어서, 전시회를 열거나 촬영을 맡는 전문가에게 잘 어울려요. 직접 높여 부를 때는 '사진작가님'이라고 해요. 간단히 '사진가'라고도 하고, 사진관에서 찍어 주는 분은 '사진사'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of someone who shoots photos as works, so it suits professionals who hold exhibitions or take commissioned shoots. To address one politely, say '사진작가님'. It can be shortened to '사진가', and a person who shoots at a photo studio is sometimes called '사진사'.

examples.ko: 사채업자에게 돈을 빌렸다가 이자 때문에 고생했어요.
examples.en: He borrowed money from a loan shark and suffered because of the interest.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 사채업자의 높은 이자가 문제라고 했어요.
examples.en: The news said the high interest of private lenders is a problem.

examples.ko: 사채업자한테 빌리면 안 된다고 부모님이 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents told me never to borrow from a private moneylender.

examples.ko: 친구가 사채업자 때문에 힘들어해서 같이 상담을 받으러 갔어요.
examples.en: My friend was struggling because of a private lender, so we went for counseling together.

examples.ko: 은행 대신 사채업자를 찾는 사람이 늘었어요.
examples.en: More people are turning to private lenders instead of banks.
The private lender keeps calling, so I feel anxious.

explain: 은행 같은 정식 금융기관이 아닌 개인에게 돈을 빌려주는 사람을 말하고, 높은 이자 때문에 좋지 않은 느낌이 있어요. '사채를 쓰다'와 함께 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 법에 따라 등록한 곳은 보통 '대부업체'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who lends money outside regular financial institutions, and it carries a negative image because of high interest. It often appears in the news with '사채를 쓰다' (to take a private loan). Registered lenders are usually called '대부업체'.

examples.ko: 마당의 소나무는 사철 푸르러서 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: The pine tree in the yard stays green all year, which looks nice.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 사철 손님이 끊이지 않아요.
examples.en: This restaurant has customers all year round.
Jeju Island has many tourists all year round.

examples.ko: 사철 입을 수 있는 얇은 재킷을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a thin jacket I can wear in every season.

examples.ko: 이 꽃은 사철 피어서 정원에 심었어요.
examples.en: This flower blooms all year, so I planted it in the garden.
Evergreen trees look pretty even in winter.

explain: '사계절'과 같은 뜻이지만 '사철 푸른 나무', '사철 내내'처럼 일 년 내내라는 뜻으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 주로 부사처럼 뒤에 서술어가 바로 와요. '농사철', '이사철'처럼 '-철'은 어떤 일이 많은 때를 말해요.
explain_en: It matches '사계절', but is often used to mean 'all year round', as in '사철 푸른 나무' or '사철 내내'. It mostly works like an adverb, followed directly by the predicate. The suffix '-철' in words like '농사철' and '이사철' marks a busy season for something.

examples.en: Designer bags are classified as luxury goods.

examples.ko: 사치품에 돈을 너무 많이 쓰지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't spend too much money on luxury goods.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 사치품에 세금을 많이 매겨요.
examples.en: This country puts heavy taxes on luxury goods.

examples.ko: 요즘은 시계도 사치품이 아니라 필수품이 됐어요.
examples.en: These days, even a watch is a necessity rather than a luxury.
It's better to save than to buy luxury goods.
In a recession, luxury goods sales drop.

explain: 꼭 필요하지 않은데 값이 비싼 물건에 쓰는 말이라서 '필수품'과 반대로 말해요. '명품'은 품질이 좋다는 긍정적인 느낌이 있지만, '사치품'은 분수에 넘친다는 느낌이 더 있어요. '사치'에 '-품'이 붙은 말이라서 '사치스럽다'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is used for expensive items you don't really need, and it is the opposite of '필수품' (necessities). '명품' sounds positive about quality, while '사치품' carries more of a 'beyond your means' feeling. It is '사치' plus '-품', so it is worth learning together with '사치스럽다'.

examples.en: Sugar can be obtained from sugar cane.

examples.ko: 사탕수수 주스를 마셔 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever tried sugar cane juice?
In warm countries, they grow a lot of sugar cane.

examples.ko: 사탕수수 밭에서 일하는 사람들을 영상으로 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw people working in a sugar cane field on a video.

examples.ko: 사탕수수 줄기를 씹으면 달콤한 물이 나와요.
examples.en: If you chew a sugar cane stalk, sweet juice comes out.
At the market, they squeeze sugar cane and sell it as juice.

explain: 이름에 '수수'가 들어가지만 곡식인 수수와는 다른 식물이에요. 설탕의 원료로 유명하고, 사탕무도 설탕의 원료가 되지만 따로 부르는 식물이에요. 한국에서 키우는 작물은 아니라서 주로 외국 이야기나 여행에서 만나요.
explain_en: Although it contains '수수', it is a different plant from sorghum, the grain. It is famous as a source of sugar; sugar beet can also make sugar but is a different plant with its own name. It isn't a common crop in Korea, so you mostly meet the word in stories about other countries or travel.

examples.ko: 사회인이 되니 시간이 정말 빨리 가요.
examples.en: Since I became a working adult, time passes really fast.
I play on an amateur adult baseball team.
After graduating from university, I took my first step as a member of society.
If you're a working adult, you must keep appointment times.
I play soccer every weekend in an adult amateur club.

examples.ko: 사회인이 되고 나서 부모님께 용돈을 드렸어요.
examples.en: After I started working, I gave my parents some pocket money.

explain: 학생을 벗어나 일하며 사회에서 활동하는 어른을 말해요. '사회인 야구', '사회인 동호회'처럼 학생이나 프로가 아닌 일반 어른이 하는 활동 앞에 자주 붙어요. 일하는 사람을 말할 때 '직장인'이 더 구체적이고, 처음 일을 시작한 사람은 '사회초년생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to an adult who has left student life and is active in society. It often comes before activities done by ordinary adults, as in '사회인 야구' or '사회인 동호회'. '직장인' is more specific for someone with a job, and a newcomer to work life is called '사회초년생'.

examples.en: The hillside neighborhood has many stairs, so it's hard to climb.
I grew up in a hillside neighborhood as a child.
The alleys of the hillside neighborhood are famous as a film location.
The night view from the hillside neighborhood is great.
It's a hillside neighborhood, so buses don't come often.

examples.ko: 할머니는 아직도 산동네 작은 집에 사세요.
examples.en: My grandmother still lives in a small house in the hillside neighborhood.

explain: 산비탈이나 높은 곳에 집이 모여 있는 동네를 말해요. 비슷한 '달동네'는 형편이 넉넉하지 않은 사람들이 사는 동네라는 느낌이 더 있어요. 계단, 골목, 야경 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It describes a neighborhood where houses cluster on a hillside or high ground. The similar word '달동네' has more of a sense of a neighborhood for people with limited means. It often appears alongside words like stairs, alleys and night view.

examples.en: The spring breeze blows softly, and I feel good.

examples.ko: 창문을 열었더니 산들산들 시원한 바람이 들어와요.
examples.en: When I opened the window, a cool, gentle breeze came in.

examples.ko: 산들산들 부는 바람에 낮잠이 솔솔 와요.
examples.en: With the gentle breeze, I get drowsy for a nap.
The cosmos flowers sway gently in the wind.
I like the soft breeze on autumn evenings.

examples.ko: 나뭇잎이 산들산들 흔들리는 걸 보고 있었어요.
examples.en: I was watching the leaves sway lightly.

explain: 세지 않고 시원하고 가볍게 부는 바람에 써요. '살랑살랑'과 비슷하지만, '산들산들'은 상쾌하고 시원한 느낌이 더 있어요. '산들산들한 바람'처럼 형용사로도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a light, cool wind that isn't strong. Similar to '살랑살랑', but '산들산들' carries more of a fresh, cool feel. It can also work as an adjective, as in '산들산들한 바람'.

examples.en: I picked and ate wild berries in the mountains.
I spread wild berry jam on bread.
In summer, the wild berries ripen red.
My grandmother made a berry syrup with wild berries.
Wild berries are sweet and sour, so kids like them.
There was a woman selling wild berries by the road.

explain: 우리가 아는 '딸기'와는 다른 종류로, 산이나 들에서 자라는 작고 새콤한 열매예요. 영어의 raspberry와 비슷한 모습이에요. 여름에 나는 과일이라 산책이나 시골 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a different kind of berry from the common '딸기' (strawberry), small and tart, growing in mountains and fields. It looks similar to a raspberry in English. It's a summer fruit, so it often comes up in walks and countryside stories.

examples.en: After dinner, I took a light stroll.
The weather is nice. Shall we go for a walk in the park?
My grandfather goes for a walk every morning.
The walking path along the river is really pretty.
I went for a stroll near the office at lunchtime.
I walked to the market as a kind of stroll.

explain: '산책'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만 요즘은 '산책'이 더 흔하고 '산보'는 조금 예스럽게 들려요. 어르신들이 많이 쓰시는 편이에요. '산보를 나가다', '산보 삼아'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '산책', but '산책' is more common today and '산보' sounds a bit old-fashioned. Older people tend to use it more. Typical phrases are '산보를 나가다' and '산보 삼아'.

examples.en: The rain stopped, so I took a stroll in the park.
I stroll along the river every evening.

examples.ko: 할머니와 함께 동네를 산보하는 시간이 좋아요.
examples.en: I like the time I spend strolling around the neighborhood with my grandmother.
I sorted out my complicated thoughts while strolling alone.
Shall we take a short walk after lunch?
I went out for a walk and ran into a friend.

explain: '산책하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 요즘은 '산책하다'가 더 흔하고, '산보하다'는 조금 예스럽게 느껴져요. 보통 '공원을 산보하다'처럼 장소에 '을/를'을 붙이거나 '산보하러 가다'로 말해요. 천천히 걸으며 여유를 즐기는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It means the same as '산책하다', but '산책하다' is more common now and '산보하다' feels a little old-fashioned. You often put the place with '을/를', as in '공원을 산보하다', or say '산보하러 가다'. It carries a relaxed feel of walking slowly and enjoying it.

examples.en: A potato field stretches across the hillside.
I was out of breath climbing the mountain slope.

examples.ko: 장마철에는 산비탈의 흙이 흘러내릴 수 있으니 조심하세요.
examples.en: During the rainy season, soil on the hillside can slide down, so be careful.
Small houses line up along the hillside.

examples.ko: 산비탈을 따라 계단식 밭이 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: Terraced fields continue along the mountain slope.
Be careful not to slip on the mountain slope.

explain: 산의 경사진 곳을 말해요. '비탈'이나 '비탈길'과 자주 같이 쓰고, 밭이나 집, 산사태 같은 이야기에서도 많이 나와요. 위쪽의 '산꼭대기', 아래쪽의 '산기슭'과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It refers to the sloped part of a mountain. It goes together with '비탈' and '비탈길', and also appears in talk about fields, houses and landslides. It's useful to learn with '산꼭대기' (summit) above and '산기슭' (foot of the mountain) below.

examples.en: The climber reached the summit carrying an oxygen tank.

examples.ko: 환자가 산소통을 옆에 두고 숨을 쉬어요.
examples.en: The patient breathes with an oxygen tank beside them.

examples.ko: 산소통이 다 떨어지기 전에 교체해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to replace the oxygen tank before it runs out.
The diver goes into the sea carrying an oxygen tank.

examples.ko: 병원에는 비상용 산소통이 항상 준비되어 있어요.
examples.en: The hospital always has emergency oxygen tanks ready.

examples.ko: 산소통 없이 높은 산에 오르는 건 위험해요.
examples.en: Climbing a high mountain without an oxygen tank is dangerous.

explain: 병원에서 쓰는 의료용, 높은 산 등반, 잠수처럼 숨쉬기 위해 산소나 공기를 담은 통을 말해요. 잠수에서는 '공기통'이라고 부르기도 해요. 의료 상황에서는 '산소호흡기', '산소 마스크'와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a tank of oxygen or air used for breathing in hospitals, high-altitude climbing and diving. In diving, it is also called '공기통'. In medical contexts it appears with words like '산소호흡기' and '산소 마스크'.

examples.en: Fog hangs around the mountainside.
I'm sweating now that I've climbed halfway up the mountain.
If you go around the mountainside, you'll find a small temple.
Clouds wrap around the middle of the mountain.

examples.ko: 산허리에 길이 나 있어서 걷기 좋아요.
examples.en: There is a path along the mountainside, so it's good for walking.
When the sun set, the mountainside turned red.

explain: 산의 중간쯤을 사람 몸의 허리에 빗대어 말하는 표현이에요. 같은 부분을 '산 중턱'이라고도 해요. 위쪽은 '산꼭대기', 아래쪽은 '산기슭'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It compares the middle part of a mountain to a person's waist. The same area is also called '산 중턱'. The top is '산꼭대기' and the bottom is '산기슭'.
